# cps-pi - Raspberry Pi 3 (and 4 / 400 with kernel8-rpi4.img)
arm_64bit=1
kernel_address=0x80000
initial_turbo=0

# HDMI always on (even if the TV is switched on later), no border, audio
hdmi_force_hotplug=1
disable_overscan=1
hdmi_drive=2
framebuffer_ignore_alpha=1

# 1080p at the CPS1 board's own refresh, 59.637 Hz (262 lines of 512 pixel
# clocks at 8 MHz): one emulated frame per refresh, nothing sped up or
# dropped. Standard 1080p timing with the pixel clock scaled to 147.6 MHz.
# No picture? Put a # in front of these four lines and remove it from the
# two standard ones below (the game then runs 0.6% fast, at 60 Hz).
hdmi_group=2
hdmi_mode=87
hdmi_timings=1920 1 88 44 148 1080 1 4 5 36 0 0 0 60 0 147602577 3
hdmi_force_mode=1
# 720p at 59.637 Hz instead: use this timings line
#hdmi_timings=1280 1 110 40 220 720 1 5 5 20 0 0 0 60 0 73801289 3

# Standard 1080p 60 Hz (720p: hdmi_mode=4)
#hdmi_group=1
#hdmi_mode=16

# Sharp pixels from the hardware scaler; name in the TV's source list
scaling_kernel=8
cec_osd_name=CPS-PI

# Fast start-up, fixed GPU clock
disable_splash=1
boot_delay=0
force_eeprom_read=0
core_freq_fixed=1

# Overclock: remove the # in front of arm_freq (heatsink needed)
[pi3]
kernel=kernel8.img
#arm_freq=1300
#over_voltage=2

[pi3+]
kernel=kernel8.img
#arm_freq=1500

[pi4]
armstub=armstub8-rpi4.bin
kernel=kernel8-rpi4.img
max_framebuffers=2
#arm_freq=1900

[all]
